# Megg

> Megg ("No seu ponto perfeito") is a free, mobile-first boiled-egg timer web app. It computes the exact cooking time from the egg's size, its starting temperature and the desired yolk doneness, then runs a countdown with an alarm. Primary language is Brazilian Portuguese (pt-BR); English and German are available in the interface. No account, no ads, no data leaves the device (the last choice is kept in localStorage).

## How it works

1. Pick the egg size, using the official Brazilian weight classes (Ministério da Agricultura): Pequeno (45–49 g), Médio (50–54 g), Grande (55–59 g), Extra (60–64 g), Jumbo (65 g +). A representative weight is used for each class (47, 52, 57, 62, 68 g).
2. Say where the egg was: in the fridge (assumed 4 °C) or out of it (room temperature slider, 8–40 °C).
3. Choose the yolk doneness: Líquida (runny), Cremosa (jammy, mollet), Firme (soft-set centre) or Cozida (fully hard-boiled).
4. Lower the egg into water that is already at a rolling boil and start the timer. Milestones on the progress bar show when each softer doneness is passed.
5. When the alarm rings, move the egg to an ice bath to stop the cooking.

## How times are computed

- Reference times are for eggs at 20 °C going into boiling water, at 58 g, 68 g and 78 g:
  - Líquida: 4:30 / 5:00 / 5:30
  - Cremosa: 6:00 / 6:30 / 7:30
  - Firme: 7:30 / 8:30 / 9:30
  - Cozida: 9:00 / 10:00 / 11:30
- Between reference weights the time is interpolated linearly. Below 58 g it is scaled by (mass / 58 g)^(2/3), because heat-penetration time grows with mass to the 2/3 power (Charles Williams' egg-boiling formula).
- Starting temperature: a fridge egg (4 °C) needs about 30 s more than a 20 °C egg, i.e. ~1.9 s per °C below 20 °C (and less time above it), scaled by the same mass factor. In hot climates an egg kept out of the fridge starts warmer and cooks faster.
- Results are rounded to the nearest 5 seconds.

## Egg science notes

- Egg white starts to set at about 62 °C and is firm at about 80 °C.
- The yolk starts to thicken at about 65 °C and is set at about 70 °C.
- Past roughly 12 minutes, iron and sulphur react and a grey-green ring forms around the yolk, with a stronger smell.
- Easier peeling: starting in boiling water helps most; an ice bath afterwards firms the egg; eggs a few days old peel better than very fresh ones. Peel under water starting from the wide end.
